options.content: Select different baseline and candidate instances. Compare workload and observation counts before interpreting rates or percentiles. Add a dashboard annotation at deployment or rollback time. No data and zero observations are unavailable, not a successful test.

panels.title: Current room users
panels.description: Match concurrent workload before comparing version behavior.

panels.title: Accepted joins · 5m
panels.description: Rolling accepted connection-event counts. Sparse traffic limits the meaning of event ratios.

panels.title: RTP ingress
panels.description: Compare publisher media workload. Receive-only calls may have no ingress.

panels.title: Joined / accepted event ratio
panels.description: Rolling event-rate ratio with at least 15 accepted events in five minutes. Events are not matched session cohorts and a ratio may exceed 100% across window boundaries.

panels.title: Peer RTT p95
panels.description: A sample-gated percentile. Compare observation counts below before interpreting differences.

panels.title: Egress loss observations
panels.description: Average sampled loss fraction. Missing observations remain unavailable.

panels.title: Ingress loss observations
panels.description: Sampled publisher loss fraction, unavailable without observations.

panels.title: Disconnects per active transport per second
panels.description: Current active transport count normalizes disconnect-event rate. It is not a per-session failure probability.

panels.title: Short closed-session share · at most 10s
panels.description: Short-session symptom. Compare closure counts and session exit reasons.

panels.title: Local forwards per ingress packet
panels.description: Fanout multiplicity. It can exceed one and is not packet-delivery efficiency.

panels.title: Output protection closes
panels.description: Session closures caused by the RTC output budget.

panels.title: Committed video policy pauses
panels.description: Committed policy pause transitions. Compare workload and user policy context.

title: o-sfu Canary Comparison
description: Compare two independently selected SFU instances over the same time range. Traffic and observation counts must be comparable before attributing differences to a deployment.
